name: Why is water coming in through my window?

mainEntity.name: Why is water coming in through my window?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water infiltration through windows often results from deteriorated caulking, damaged window frames, or worn-out weather stripping that allows water to penetrate during rain. Clogged window sills or drainage channels can also cause water to pool and overflow into the interior. In some cases, issues with the building's exterior siding or roofing above the window can direct water towards the window, leading to leaks. Identifying the exact entry point is crucial for an effective repair.
acceptedAnswer.description: Water typically enters through damaged caulking, frames, weather stripping, or clogged drainage. Problems with exterior siding or roofing can also contribute to leaks.
